Customer Churn and Loyalty Analysis¶

Streamflow is a fictitious company created for the purpose of this analytics project, and the customer data used has been synthetically generated.
The goal is to provide a realistic context for modern customer analytics; demonstrating the type of data, features, and challenges that would be present in a real world digital learning platform.

Company Overview:
Streamflow is a subscription-based digital learning platform that offers online courses and professional certificates to a global customer base. The company delivers flexible subscription tiers, enables users to purchase add-ons, and tracks rich engagement and loyalty signals across its entire user base.

What kind of customers and data are involved?

  • Customers come from a variety of countries and industries to mimic international usage.
  • Users select between subscription types such as “Basic” and “Free,” with the option for paying for additional premium options.
  • Each user can complete courses, earn certificates and collect loyalty points based on their usage. The loyalty point accumulation can be very complex due to the specific nature of the business, the targeted demographics or simply if the business rules are highly specific based on other cost/benefit analyses. It also depends on dynamic program/incentives structure so we will not get into that here.
  • The data contains key engagement and product usage metrics: average weekly hours, tenure, number of courses completed, engagement score, monthly spend, add-ons purchased, etc.
  • Customer support activity and payment behaviors are monitored to help flag risk and drive retention efforts.

All analysis in this project is built on the synthetic customer dataset I created, made to mimic what a company like Streamflow would collect in a true production setting but can easily be adapted to your business needs. See below on how I can easily adapt this for you and feel free to reach out to me if you have specific additions/modifications or data manipulation needs. I have extended this analysis for demo purposes into a dashboard as well. Refer to my website for the Streamlit based demo dashboard, built using this data.

Engagement & Usage Patterns¶

Now we analyze how our customers use StreamFlow: time spent on the platform, courses completed, and how these relate to subscription types and loyalty.

Observation:
Engagement increases dramatically with each higher subscription tier.

  • Premium and Enterprise users are consistently more engaged, but a small set of Basic and Free users also achieve high engagement which is usually a key upsell target.

What this shows:
Premium and Enterprise customers use StreamFlow 4–8x more each week than Free or Basic users.
This underscores both the value of upsell and the risk if high engagement users churn.

Insight:
There’s a strong positive correlation between engagement and loyalty points across all segments.

  • Power users accumulate significant loyalty points, but some engaged Basic users lag behind which is important for marketing campaigns or feature improvements.

Takeaway:

  • Enterprise and Premium customers complete the most courses, and course completion rises with tenure across all segments.
  • For Basic users, early plateau suggests that there might be an opportunity for targeted engagement campaigns within the first year.

Churn & Retention Analysis¶

Customer churn is a critical metric for companies like this one who offer tiered services which can be opted out of:
The following visuals break down where, when, and why customers churn and who our highest retention segments are.

Observation:

  • Churn is highest for Free users, and decreases relatively sharply with each higher subscription tier.
  • Enterprise churn is extremely low Retention is highest in our most valuable accounts.

Insight:

  • The risk of churn is highest for new customers. Churn rate declines rapidly as tenure increases. This means customers who remain for a year or more are much less likely to leave.
  • Action: Focus onboarding resources on the first 6–12 months to maximize long-term retention.

Key Takeaway:

  • Engaged users rarely churn So, the median engagement score for churned users is much lower than that for retained users.
  • Predicting churn early is possible using engagement metrics and tenure together, and that's our goal to find out.

Actionable Insights:

  • Low engagement score, high support tickets, low loyalty, and missed payments are the most predictive of churn.
  • Targeted retention campaigns and proactive outreach for these risk factors can improve LTV (life-time-value).

Churn & Engagement by Country¶

Insight:

  • Some countries (like India, Brazil) have higher churn and lower engagement, while US/CA seem to be more stable.
  • Engagement varies by country and so localizing onboarding or features and make them specfic to different reagions/countries should be considered.

NPS Score Distribution by Subscription Type and Churn¶

Insight:

  • Churned customers report lower NPS across all segments.
  • Highest NPS is found among retained Premium/Enterprise customers, which makes sense and shows that satisfaction and loyalty are important to retain future customers.
  • We should target low-NPS cohorts for proactive outreach.

Support Tickets vs. Churn by Subscription Type¶

Insight:

  • Enterprise users submit the most support tickets, but have the lowest churn.
  • For Free/Basic users, high support tickets are a strong predictor of churn (possible frustration).
  • Action: we should focus on improving support experience for lower-tier users if posssible.

Loyalty Points & Add-ons: Impact on Churn and Revenue¶

Insight:

  • Higher loyalty points and more add-ons are both associated with lower churn.
  • Upsell/cross-sell strategies and loyalty program engagement directly seem to improve retention.

Enterprise Industry Deep Dive¶

Insight:

  • Some industries (e.g., Tech, Healthcare) may have lower churn and higher NPS—target for expansion.
  • Action: Prioritize Customer Success resources in industries with higher churn or low NPS.

Executive Summary: Key Customer Insights So Far¶

StreamFlow Inc. Customer Analysis — Business Takeaways

  • User Base: The majority are Basic or Free users; Premium and Enterprise.
  • Engagement: Higher tier customers are far more engaged in both in usage and courses completed. Some Free/Basic users show high engagement (this group seems to be the prime upsell target).
  • Loyalty & NPS: Loyalty points and high NPS scores are strongly linked to retention, especially in paid plans. Churned customers consistently report lower NPS which seems as expected.
  • Churn: Churn rates are highest for free users and in the first few months of tenure. Churn declines as tenure increases which again is expected and makes sense here.
  • Geography: Countries like India, Brazil, and South Africa have higher churn and lower engagement than US/CA, suggesting regional strategy is needed.
  • Support: Enterprise users seem to submit more support tickets but are also less likely to churn. For Free/Basic users, high support tickets are a warning sign for churn—possible frustration.
  • Loyalty Programs & Add-ons: Higher loyalty correlates with lower churn, reconfirming the value of cross-sell and engagement programs/initiatives are a key user for this business.
  • Enterprise Segments: In Enterprise accounts, Education and Retail industries seem to show the lowest churn and highest NPS. So we now know which is our stickiest cohort.

Customer Segmentation Summary¶

  • To better understand our customer base, we will be clustering to segment users into distinct groups based on features including engagement score, loyalty points, monthly spend, number of courses completed, add-ons purchased, and churn status.

  • After scaling these variables, we identified four key segments using k-means clustering. (python begins at 0 thus the clusters as well. This can be easily renamed if need. We dont need to do that since the numerical value for the cluster is simply a name being given for a reference here such as A, B, C etc'

  • This allows us to move beyond simple averages and spot meaningful behavioral patterns in the data.

  • By analyzing the profiles and needs of each cluster, we can tailor retention, upsell, and support strategies to maximize impact.

  • The segment highlights below summarize the main characteristics and opportunities for each group.

  • Cluster 0: Premium Loyalists

    • 56% Premium, 17% Enterprise
    • Most engaged, highest loyalty, lowest churn
    • Retention and upsell are the key factorts for this cluster. We should maximize advocacy & referrals for them

  • Cluster 1: Value Seekers

    • 53% Free, 27% Basic
    • Lowest engagement & loyalty, highest churn
    • Onboard, educate, and target for upgrades due to their high churn risk. OIffer special discounts if needed. If we can keep them for longer, they'll be much more likely to be retained and upgrade to a higher tier.

  • Cluster 2: Up-and-Coming Engagers

    • 53% Basic, 35% Premium
    • Growing engagement & loyalty, medium/low churn
    • Prime upsell and rewards targets. We do need to convert Basics to Premium but they seems to like the product and may not need personlized discounts. Regardless, we need to retain them and may benefit from personalized offers based on current usage.

  • Cluster 3: Support-Heavy/Complex

    • 42% Enterprise, 36% Premium
    • High support needs, mixed engagement, elevated churn
    • Proactive support and product improvements are needed for this cluster. They've already invested in our product but we need to provide higher quality of support/customization to not let them leave. So, high paying bunch but they're very sensitive to inadequate support or other issues with our product that we need resolve or probe them on to understand what is not working well.

Final Executive Summary¶

  • 23,000 customers analyzed
  • Churn rate: 28.3%
  • Premium users: 31.2%
  • Highly engaged: 3.2% score >35 engagement
  • Top loyalty: 24.9% in top-25% points
  • Support-heavy: 66.5% logged >2 tickets recently
  • Churn remains highest among low-engagement users and Free/Basic plans—upgrading and onboarding efforts here will drive the biggest retention gains.
  • Highly engaged and loyal users are most likely to be Premium or Enterprise, with the lowest churn and highest potential for advocacy and upsell.
  • A sizable segment requires frequent support—flag for proactive service improvements or product guidance.
  • Cluster profiles provide an actionable roadmap for marketing, customer success, and revenue teams.

Cohort Analysis: Changes in Customer KPIs Over Time¶

To assess how user metrics are evolving, I compare customers who joined in the last 6 months with those who joined 7–12 months ago.
This approach highlights shifts in churn, engagement, premium adoption, loyalty, and support load between recent and earlier cohorts.

Cohort KPI Summary¶

  Cohort Count Churn Rate Premium % Engaged % Loyalty Top 25% Support-Heavy %
0 Recent (0–6 mo) 1774 35.0% 30.8% 8.2% 40.0% 18.9%
1 Earlier (7–12 mo) 1469 29.5% 31.9% 6.5% 34.4% 27.5%

Change Highlights¶

Below is a summary of how key metrics differ between new and older user cohorts.

Metric Changes (Recent – Earlier):¶

  • Churn rate: 35.0% (+5.5%)
  • Premium %: 30.8% (-1.1%)
  • Engaged %: 8.2% (+1.6%)
  • Loyalty Top 25%: 40.0% (+5.6%)
  • Support-heavy %: 18.9% (-8.6%)

Interpretation:

  • Increased churn in the recent cohort suggests onboarding or early experience may need improvement.
  • A rise in Premium adoption or engagement is a positive signal for product growth.
  • More support-heavy users in the latest cohort could indicate new friction points or increased usage complexity.

This analysis helps prioritize which parts of the user journey or product should be reviewed next.

Segment-Level Revenue and Retention¶

To understand which customer groups drive value, I break down average monthly revenue and churn rate by cluster.
This clarifies which segments contribute most to the business and where retention efforts will have the biggest financial impact.

Revenue & Churn by Segment¶

  cluster Customers Avg_Monthly_Spend Total_Monthly_Revenue Churn_Rate Revenue_Share
0 0 5095 $41.73 $212,628 21.3% 41.0%
1 1 7488 $10.37 $77,669 33.3% 15.0%
2 2 2535 $50.13 $127,069 18.8% 24.5%
3 3 7882 $12.90 $101,686 31.0% 19.6%

Key Findings:

  • The segment with the highest revenue share and lowest churn is the most valuable; focus retention and expansion efforts here.
  • Segments with high churn and lower spend may require improved onboarding or more targeted upsell offers.
  • Low revenue but high churn segments may be candidates for reengagement or cost optimization efforts.

Recommended Actions¶

    1. Prioritize retention for Cluster 0 (drives 41.0% of monthly revenue with 21.3% churn).
    1. Target re-engagement campaigns for Cluster 1 (highest churn rate at 33.3%).
    1. Review onboarding or marketing for low-revenue, high-churn clusters (1, 3).

Cluster Highlights¶

  • Cluster 0: 5095.0 users, avg monthly spend 41.73, churn rate 21.3%, revenue share 41.0%. → Strong revenue, but monitor churn closely.
  • Cluster 1: 7488.0 users, avg monthly spend 10.37, churn rate 33.3%, revenue share 15.0%. → High churn risk; target with onboarding or re-engagement.
  • Cluster 2: 2535.0 users, avg monthly spend 50.13, churn rate 18.8%, revenue share 24.5%. → Strong revenue, but monitor churn closely.
  • Cluster 3: 7882.0 users, avg monthly spend 12.90, churn rate 31.0%, revenue share 19.6%. → High churn risk; target with onboarding or re-engagement.

These short summaries help us quickly see which segments are driving revenue, retention, or risk—making it easier to prioritize where we focus our next actions or campaigns.

StreamFlow Interactive Insights Dashboard (Full Streamlit App)¶

How to Use the Streamlit Dashboard¶

To make our advanced analytics accessible to everyone, I've created a fully interactive dashboard using Streamlit. Please refer to the Streamlit project on my website, under the projects section (https://aryankaushik89.github.io/). This web app lets you upload your customer data, visualize key metrics, explore segments, and see AI-generated business insights. For the demo, we load in the synthetic data we created for this analysis and use that to showcase what can be shown on a dashboard.

All recommendations update automatically as you upload new data and when you change filters. So, right now in the demo dashboard (which you can access via my website or GitHub), you are able to see how changing filters will regenerate automatic, rules-based insights depending on what is being output in the dashboard. But the best part is that you're able to pass an API key for any LLM of your preference and have the insights generated for your specific data and/or filters you have applied in the dashboard. Then, in the 'Connect LLM' tab, you will see AI-generated insights dynamically.

In terms of the data to be used, refer to the About tab and rename matching column names to what is expected in the app to make the dashboard work easily. Alternatively, email me (aryan23.kaushik@gmail.com) or contact me via LinkedIn and I can easily develop this dashboard for your specific data types. Even better, with some brief instructions or a dictionary of your particular fields in your data, I can customize the dashboard for your needs. If you want to use this dashboard as is and make your own changes, see the footnote on any tab that will direct you to my GitHub with the raw code.
